original_failure.observed: TestAstraSidecarInheritedPipeCannotDefeatDeadline failed at 736.0433ms against a 600ms wall-clock assertion with context deadline exceeded.

diagnosis.finding: The old test conflated Windows process startup/scheduler wall-clock with the inherited-pipe drain mechanism. The behavior to assert is exec.ErrWaitDelay while the direct child has exited successfully but a descendant still holds inherited stdout/stderr. Context cancellation is covered separately by the sidecar timeout test.
diagnosis.test_change: The fixture context is long enough not to race Windows startup; the assertion now requires errors.Is(err, exec.ErrWaitDelay) and ctx.Err()==nil. This is a mechanism assertion, not a relaxed elapsed-time threshold.

controlled_checks.observed: 10/10 runs returned exec: WaitDelay expired before I/O complete; measured CallSidecar times were approximately 668-875ms and context did not expire.

limits: This closes the false-negative regression check. It does not change the production CallSidecar implementation.

The module checkpoint is local/ahead of its remote by one commit; release integration must decide whether this test-only checkpoint is published or whether the consumer remains pinned to the already verified production-code commit.
